meta.title: Operational Resilience in Schools — Benchmarking Scoring Model
meta.project: ABSA x Bounce Readiness — Operational Resilience Benchmarking (AU/NZ, 2026)

scoringRules.single: Score = rating of the one selected answer.
scoringRules.sum_all: Score = sum of ratings of every ticked answer.
scoringRules.erp_conditional: If the option flagged isOverride (Emergency Response Plan / Emergency Management Plan) is selected, score = its rating (20) and all other selected options are ignored. If it is NOT selected, score = sum of ratings of the other selected options.
scoringRules.none: Not scored — profile / incident-history / self-assessment / emerging-risk questions. Captured for the report and segmentation only.

meta.howToScore: total=0; for each scored question: single -> total += rating(selected); sum_all -> total += sum(rating(o) for o in selected); erp_conditional -> total += (rating(override) if override selected else sum(rating(o) for o in selected if not o.isOverride)). Map total into maturityLevels by [minInclusive, nextMin). Repeat per section using sections[].anchors for the domain radar.
notes: Overall maturity = sum of every SCORED question's earned rating, mapped to a band in maturityLevels.
Band boundaries were derived by summing the per-question levelAnchors; they equal [105, 285, 332.5, 364, 392.5].
Boundary convention: a level owns scores >= its minInclusive and < the next level's minInclusive (lower bound inclusive). e.g. exactly 285 => Level 3. Confirm the tie-break with the client if needed.

sections[].anchors let you compute per-DOMAIN maturity the same way: sum a section's earned score and compare to that section's L1..L5 anchors (for the dashboard radar / 'rating against best practice').
A null rating means the option carries no points (treat as 0). Some options on unscored questions still carry feedback text — keep it for the report even though it does not affect the score.

DATA FLAGS TO CONFIRM WITH CLIENT: (1) Q32 reads like a maturity question but every rating is blank in the sheet, so it is currently unscored. (2) The sum of the maximum answer rating per scored question is 367.5, below the 392.5 anchor ceiling — decide which is the denominator for any % / progress display. (3) Option labels must match exactly what MS Forms submits; normalize whitespace/newlines before matching (e.g. Q35 labels contain line breaks).

maturityLevels.label: Reactive
maturityLevels.fullLabel: Level 1 – Reactive (minimal planning, ad hoc response)

maturityLevels.label: Integrated
maturityLevels.fullLabel: Level 4 – Integrated (aligned EM, CIM, BC systems)

questions.text: Which best describes your school?
What is your role?
How many students are enrolled at your school?
Approximately how many staff work at your school?
What is your School type?
Which year levels does your school serve?
In which country is your school located?
Which Australian State or Territory is your school in?
Which NZ region is your school in?
Where is your school located?
Which of the following best describes your campus arrangement?
Who has primary responsibility for operational resilience within your school?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Principal / Head of School
options.feedback: Document resilience ownership in the Principal / Head of School's role description and the school's resilience policy. Consider delegating day-to-day coordination to a nominated deputy while retaining executive accountability, and establish clear reporting lines to the Board / Council.

options.label: Leadership / Executive Team
options.feedback: Clarify which individual within the Leadership / Executive Team holds primary accountability for resilience to avoid diffusion of responsibility. Document this ownership in role descriptions and the resilience policy, and ensure regular reporting to the Board / Council on resilience activities and outcomes.

options.label: Business Manager / School Business Administrator
options.feedback: Formally document the Business Manager / School Business Administrator's responsibility for resilience, ensure it is supported by the Principal, and establish clear escalation pathways. Regular reporting to the Leadership Team and Board / Council will strengthen governance oversight.

options.label: Risk / Compliance Lead
options.feedback: Ensure the Risk / Compliance Lead has sufficient authority and access to leadership to drive preparedness initiatives effectively. Document the responsibility formally, establish clear reporting lines to the Executive and Board / Council, and ensure adequate time allocation for resilience activities alongside other compliance duties.

options.label: Shared responsibility
options.feedback: Assign primary accountability for resilience to a single individual (such as the Principal, Business Manager, or Risk Lead) while maintaining shared involvement across the leadership team. Document this ownership in role descriptions and the school's resilience policy to ensure clarity and accountability.

options.label: Unsure or no one
options.feedback: Assign primary responsibility for resilience to an appropriate senior leader (such as the Principal, Business Manager, or Risk Lead) and document this in their role description and the school's resilience policy. Communicate this ownership to staff and establish reporting lines to ensure accountability.

options.label: Other
options.feedback: Ensure whoever holds primary responsibility for operational resilience has appropriate seniority, authority, and access to leadership. Document the responsibility formally in role descriptions and the school's resilience policy. Establish clear reporting lines to the Executive and Board / Council, and ensure the role is resourced with adequate time and support.

questions.text: Does your school have a formal committee responsible for emergency preparedness and resilience?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: Ensure the Emergency Planning Committee meets regularly (at least quarterly), maintains documented terms of reference, and includes representatives from key operational areas. Review committee membership annually and track actions to completion.

options.label: No
options.feedback: Establish an Emergency Planning Committee with at least two members, including the Chief Warden, Facilities Manager, and representatives from key areas such as boarding, sports, and student services. This committee can be integrated with existing forums such as your WHS/OHS Committee or Leadership Team. Define terms of reference, meeting frequency, and reporting lines.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Clarify whether a formal committee exists with responsibility for emergency preparedness and resilience. If one exists, ensure its role, membership, and meeting schedule are clearly documented and communicated. If not, establish an Emergency Planning Committee with at least two members and define terms of reference.

questions.text: How often is operational resilience discussed by senior leadership?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Monthly
options.feedback: Include review of key risk indicators, incident trends, exercise outcomes, and progress on improvement actions in leadership resilience discussions. Consider incorporating mini desktop scenarios quarterly to test decision-making capabilities.

options.label: Quarterly
options.feedback: Increase leadership resilience discussions to monthly to enable more responsive decision-making, particularly during periods of elevated risk. Ensure each session covers key risks, recent incidents or near-misses, exercise outcomes, and accountability for improvement actions.

options.label: Annually
options.feedback: Increase leadership resilience discussions to at least quarterly, establishing operational resilience as a standing agenda item. Include updates on risk trends, incident learnings, exercise outcomes, and progress on improvement initiatives.

options.label: Only following incidents
options.feedback: Establish a regular cadence (start with six-monthly, progressing to quarterly) for proactive resilience discussions. This shift from reactive to planned engagement enables leadership to identify emerging risks, allocate resources effectively, and drive continuous improvement.

options.label: Never
options.feedback: Establish operational resilience as a standing agenda item for leadership meetings, starting with six-monthly then progressing to quarterly. Include updates on emergency preparedness, business continuity, incident trends, and improvement actions. Document decisions and assign accountability.

questions.text: How often does the Board / Council receive resilience-related reporting?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Monthly
options.feedback: Ensure Board / Council resilience reports include key risk indicators, incident summaries, exercise outcomes, and progress on improvement actions. Periodically review the report format to maintain engagement and relevance.

options.label: Quarterly
options.feedback: Consider increasing Board / Council reporting to monthly to enable more timely governance decisions, particularly during periods of heightened risk or following significant incidents. Ensure reports capture key risk trends, incident outcomes, and progress on resilience initiatives.

options.label: Annually
options.feedback: Increase Board / Council reporting to at least quarterly, including updates on key risks, incident trends, exercise outcomes, and improvement actions. Regular reporting strengthens governance and demonstrates commitment to operational resilience.

options.label: Ad hoc
options.feedback: Establish a regular reporting schedule (at least quarterly) for Board / Council updates on resilience activities, risks, and improvement initiatives. Structured reporting ensures the Board remains informed and can fulfil governance responsibilities effectively.

options.label: Never
options.feedback: Establish a formal reporting mechanism to provide at least annual (preferably quarterly) Board / Council updates on operational resilience, including emergency preparedness, business continuity, and critical incident management.

questions.text: Leadership actively supports preparedness initiatives
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Strongly Disagree
options.feedback: Engage leadership through a brief presentation on resilience risks and benefits. Start with quick wins to demonstrate value.

options.label: Disagree
options.feedback: Identify barriers to leadership engagement. Consider linking resilience to strategic priorities or compliance obligations.

options.label: Neutral
options.feedback: Build leadership support by demonstrating how preparedness initiatives reduce risk and protect the school's reputation.

options.label: Agree
options.feedback: Encourage leadership to visibly champion resilience initiatives and participate in exercises.

options.label: Strongly Agree
options.feedback: Maintain leadership engagement through regular updates and involvement in exercises and planning.

questions.text: Resilience is integrated into strategic planning
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Strongly Disagree
options.feedback: Include resilience as a standing item in strategic planning. Link preparedness to long-term school sustainability.

options.label: Disagree
options.feedback: Advocate for resilience considerations in strategic discussions. Highlight how disruptions impact strategic objectives.

options.label: Neutral
options.feedback: Strengthen the connection between resilience and strategy by identifying how key risks could affect strategic goals.

options.label: Agree
options.feedback: Ensure resilience is explicitly referenced in strategic plans with defined objectives and accountability.

options.label: Strongly Agree
options.feedback: Continue to align resilience initiatives with strategic priorities and review annually.

questions.text: Roles and responsibilities are clearly defined
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Strongly Disagree
options.feedback: Document key resilience roles in position descriptions and emergency plans. Communicate responsibilities to all staff.

options.label: Disagree
options.feedback: Review and clarify resilience roles. Ensure wardens, incident teams, and coordinators have documented responsibilities.

options.label: Neutral
options.feedback: Formalise role definitions and ensure staff understand their responsibilities through training and documentation.

options.label: Agree
options.feedback: Review resilience roles annually and after exercises to ensure they remain current and understood.

options.label: Strongly Agree
options.feedback: Maintain role clarity through regular reviews, onboarding processes, and exercise participation.

questions.text: How often are your emergency management arrangements formally reviewed?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

questions.text: Which emergency plans do you currently maintain?
questions.scoringComment: If ERP ticked, do not add in points for the other ones. If ERP not selected, then add all other points

options.label: Emergency Response Plan / Emergency Management Plan
options.feedback: Ensure the Emergency Response Plan is clearly documented, easily accessible, and includes all relevant procedures (evacuation, lockdown, shelter-in-place, medical emergencies). Review annually and after any incidents or site changes.

options.label: Lockdown Procedures
options.feedback: Develop a comprehensive Emergency Response Plan that consolidates all emergency procedures into a single, coordinated document.

options.label: Evacuation Procedures
options.feedback: Develop a comprehensive Emergency Response Plan that consolidates all emergency procedures into a single, coordinated document.

options.label: Shelter-in-Place Procedures
options.feedback: Develop a comprehensive Emergency Response Plan that consolidates all emergency procedures into a single, coordinated document.

options.label: Medical Emergency Procedures
options.feedback: Develop a comprehensive Emergency Response Plan that consolidates all emergency procedures into a single, coordinated document.

options.label: None of the above
options.feedback: Develop a comprehensive Emergency Response Plan covering evacuation, lockdown, shelter-in-place, and medical emergency procedures as a priority.

questions.text: How confident are you that staff understand their role during an emergency?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Not confident
options.feedback: Prioritise staff training and clear communication of emergency roles. Conduct regular drills and provide accessible reference materials.

options.label: Slightly confident
options.feedback: Increase training frequency and ensure all staff receive role-specific guidance. Use drills to reinforce understanding.

options.label: Moderately confident
options.feedback: Build staff confidence through more frequent exercises and post-drill debriefs. Address any gaps identified during practice.

options.label: Very confident
options.feedback: Continue regular training and use exercises to maintain confidence and identify improvement areas.

options.label: Extremely confident
options.feedback: Maintain staff confidence through ongoing training, regular exercises, and clear onboarding processes for new staff.

questions.text: How frequently are emergency training and exercises conducted at your K-12 campus (excluding ELC)?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Never / greater than 2 years ago
options.feedback: Establish a regular exercise program immediately. Start with basic evacuation and lockdown drills and progress to other scenarios.

options.label: Every two years
options.feedback: Increase emergency exercise frequency to at least annual. Regular practice builds muscle memory and identifies gaps before real incidents.

options.label: Annual
options.feedback: Consider increasing emergency exercises to twice yearly to cover different scenarios and maintain staff readiness throughout the year.

options.label: Twice Yearly
options.feedback: Vary scenarios and variables across exercises and use debriefs to drive continuous improvement. Consider conducting drills during recess / lunch, incorporating casualties, refusals and mobility impairments.

options.label: Quarterly
options.feedback: Maintain variety in exercise scenarios and continue to incorporate lessons learned. Consider conducting drills during recess / lunch, incorporating casualties, refusals and mobility impairments.

questions.text: After drills or exercises, are findings documented and used to improve arrangements?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Yes, consistently
options.feedback: Continue capturing lessons learned from exercises and tracking actions to completion. Share insights with staff to reinforce learning.

options.label: Sometimes
options.feedback: Formalise the debrief process. Document findings after every exercise and assign accountability for improvement actions.

options.label: Rarely
options.feedback: Introduce a standard debrief template and process. Without documentation, valuable lessons are lost and the same issues recur.

options.label: Never
options.feedback: Establish a formal debrief process for all exercises. Document observations, identify improvements, and track actions to completion.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Confirm whether debriefs occur and findings are recorded. If not, implement a simple process to capture and act on lessons learned.

questions.text: Are your school evacuation diagrams up to date (updated within last 5 years or after site changes)?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Yes, all current
options.feedback: Continue to review evacuation diagrams after any site changes and ensure they are clearly displayed in all buildings.

options.label: Some are current
options.feedback: Prioritise updating outdated evacuation diagrams. Ensure all buildings have current, clearly displayed evacuation routes and assembly points.

options.label: No
options.feedback: Update all evacuation diagrams as a priority. Ensure they reflect current layouts, exits, and assembly points. Display prominently in all areas.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Conduct an audit of all evacuation diagrams. Identify outdated or missing diagrams and schedule updates to ensure compliance and clarity.

questions.text: Does your school have a Critical Incident (Crisis) Management Plan or equivalent?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Yes, current
options.feedback: Ensure the Critical Incident Management Plan is tested through regular desktop exercises, reviewed annually, and that the Critical Incident Management Team is trained in its use. Confirm the plan covers escalation protocols, communications, and recovery.

options.label: Yes, but needs updating
options.feedback: Prioritise updating the Critical Incident Management Plan. Review team roles, contact details, escalation protocols, and communication templates. Test through desktop exercises and train the team in its application.

options.label: No
options.feedback: Develop a Critical Incident Management Plan as a priority. Include incident assessment and escalation protocols, defined team roles, stakeholder communications, and recovery planning. Establish a Critical Incident Management Team and conduct regular training and exercises.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Confirm whether a Critical Incident Management Plan exists and assess its currency. If no plan exists, develop one covering escalation, team roles, communications, and recovery. Ensure the team is trained and the plan is tested through exercises.

questions.text: Does your school have a designated Critical Incident (Crisis) Management Team?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: Ensure Critical Incident Management Team members are trained, understand their roles, and participate in regular exercises to maintain readiness.

options.label: No
options.feedback: Establish a Critical Incident Management Team with defined roles. Include senior leadership and key functional representatives.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Clarify whether a formal Critical Incident Management Team exists. If not, establish one with clear membership, roles, and activation procedures.

questions.text: How often does your Critical Incident Management Team undertake training in managing an incident?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Quarterly
options.feedback: Maintain quarterly CIMT training frequency and vary training content to cover different incident types and team functions.

options.label: Six monthly
options.feedback: Ensure CIMT training covers a range of scenarios and includes all team members, including deputies and alternates.

options.label: Annually
options.feedback: Consider increasing CIMT training to six-monthly to maintain team readiness. Supplement with desktop exercises between formal training sessions.

options.label: Every two years
options.feedback: Increase CIMT training frequency to at least annually. Infrequent training leads to skill decay and reduced confidence during real incidents.

options.label: We have conducted training over two years ago
options.feedback: Schedule CIMT refresher training as a priority. Skills and knowledge fade without regular practice, impacting team effectiveness.

options.label: Not completed
options.feedback: Implement CIMT training as a priority. Training builds confidence, clarifies roles, and prepares the team to respond effectively.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Confirm CIMT training history and establish a regular schedule. Aim for at least annual training to maintain team capability.

questions.text: How often does your Critical Incident Management Team undertake desktop exercising?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Quarterly
options.feedback: Vary desktop exercise scenarios (e.g., student fatality, cyber attack, bushfire) to build broad capability and test different aspects of the plan.

options.label: Six monthly
options.feedback: Ensure desktop exercises test different scenarios and involve all CIMT members. Use debriefs to identify improvements.

options.label: Annually
options.feedback: Consider increasing desktop exercises to six-monthly. Desktop exercises are low-cost and highly effective for testing plans and building team confidence.

options.label: Every two years
options.feedback: Increase desktop exercise frequency to at least annually. Regular practice identifies plan gaps and builds team confidence before real incidents occur.

options.label: We have conducted training over two years ago
options.feedback: Schedule a desktop exercise as a priority. Extended gaps between exercises mean plans remain untested and teams unprepared.

options.label: Not completed
options.feedback: Conduct a desktop exercise as a priority. This is the most effective way to test the plan, identify gaps, and build team readiness.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Confirm desktop exercise history and establish a regular schedule. Desktop exercises are essential for testing plans and team preparedness.

questions.text: How prepared is your school to manage various critical incident scenarios (e.g. student fatality, cyber attack, bushfire)?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Not Prepared
options.feedback: Prioritise developing the Critical Incident Management Plan and team. Start with the highest-risk scenarios and build capability progressively.

options.label: Slightly
options.feedback: Identify gaps in current critical incident preparedness. Focus on developing plans, training the team, and conducting exercises for key scenarios.

options.label: Moderately
options.feedback: Continue building critical incident capability through regular training and exercises. Test plans against a variety of scenarios to identify improvement areas.

options.label: Well Prepared
options.feedback: Maintain critical incident readiness through regular exercises, plan reviews, and team training. Consider emerging risks in planning.

options.label: Highly Prepared
options.feedback: Continue regular exercises, incorporate lessons learned, and stay current with emerging risks and best practice.

questions.text: During an incident, what systems are available to support decision-making?

options.label: Consider implementing at least basic incident logging and communication tools. Even simple systems like incident log templates and Teams channels improve coordination during incidents.

questions.text: What does your Critical Incident Management Plan contain?
questions.scoringComment: Total each ticked, comment will be if only a few of the items are ticked

options.label: Incident assessment and escalation protocols
options.feedback: Review the Critical Incident Management Plan against this checklist and prioritise adding any missing elements: incident assessment and escalation protocols, defined leadership roles, stakeholder communications processes, pre-scripted templates, media/reputational considerations, parent/guardian reunification arrangements, staging area protocols, meeting agenda templates, information management protocols, SITREP templates, and recovery planning.

questions.text: Does your school have a documented Business Continuity Plan, continuity framework, or equivalent?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Yes, current
options.feedback: Ensure the Business Continuity Plan is reviewed at least annually, tested through exercises, and covers critical functions including teaching and learning, student welfare, administration, facilities, and other business units. Confirm staff are aware of their roles and that recovery priorities are clearly defined.

options.label: Yes, but needs updating
options.feedback: Prioritise updating the Business Continuity Plan to reflect current operations, systems, and contacts. Review critical function priorities, recovery timeframes, and resource requirements. Communicate changes to relevant staff and test through a desktop exercise.

options.label: No
options.feedback: Develop a Business Continuity Plan as a priority. Identify critical school functions (teaching and learning, student welfare, administration, facilities, and other business units) and the resources required to maintain or restore them. Document recovery priorities, timeframes, and responsibilities.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Confirm whether a documented Business Continuity Plan exists. If one exists, locate it and assess its currency. If not, develop one to ensure the school can maintain critical operations during disruptions and recover effectively.

questions.text: Has your school completed a Business Impact Analysis?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Completed and updated annually
options.feedback: Continue to review the Business Impact Analysis annually, particularly after significant changes to systems, staffing, or service delivery. Use BIA findings to inform resource allocation and recovery strategies.

options.label: Completed but not updated in the last 2 years
options.feedback: Review the Business Impact Analysis to ensure it reflects current operations, systems, and dependencies. Reassess critical functions, recovery timeframes, and resource requirements, then update the Business Continuity Plan accordingly.

options.label: Started but not finished
options.feedback: Prioritise completing the Business Impact Analysis. Identify remaining critical functions to assess, document dependencies and recovery timeframes, and use the findings to strengthen the Business Continuity Plan.

options.label: No
options.feedback: Conduct a Business Impact Analysis to identify critical functions and understand the consequences of disruption. Start by listing key functions across teaching, student welfare, administration, and facilities, then assess the impact of their unavailability over time.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Confirm whether a Business Impact Analysis has been completed. If one exists, assess its currency. If not, conduct a BIA to identify critical functions, dependencies, and recovery priorities.

questions.text: How prepared is your school to continue/recover essential operations following disruption (e.g. boarding facility loss, cyber attack, ICT outage)?

options.label: n/a
options.feedback: Consider whether business continuity preparedness applies to the school context. Most schools face potential disruptions to facilities, technology, or operations that would benefit from continuity planning.

options.label: Not Prepared
options.feedback: Prioritise developing a Business Continuity Plan, conduct a Business Impact Analysis to identify critical functions, and establish recovery procedures for likely scenarios such as ICT outages, facility loss, or cyber incidents.

options.label: Slightly
options.feedback: Review the Business Continuity Plan (or develop one if not in place), ensure critical functions are documented with recovery procedures, and test arrangements through desktop exercises. Focus on high-impact scenarios relevant to the school.

options.label: Moderately
options.feedback: Review the Business Continuity Plan for completeness, ensure recovery procedures are documented and tested, and address any gaps identified through exercises or near-miss incidents.

options.label: Well Prepared
options.feedback: Continue to maintain and test the Business Continuity Plan regularly. Ensure arrangements remain current as operations, systems, and staff change. Use exercises and incident reviews to identify improvement opportunities.

options.label: Highly Prepared
options.feedback: Maintain strong business continuity preparedness through regular plan reviews, ongoing testing, and continuous improvement. Consider how emerging risks (such as evolving cyber threats) may require adaptation of arrangements.

questions.text: Has your school tested its business continuity or recovery arrangements in the past 24 months?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Tested annually
options.feedback: Continue varying business continuity exercise scenarios and exercise types (desktop, functional, full-scale) to test different aspects of arrangements. Document lessons learned and track improvement actions to completion.

options.label: Tested between 1 and 2 years ago
options.feedback: Schedule a business continuity test within the next six months to validate current procedures, contact details, and recovery capabilities. Consider a desktop exercise as an efficient way to re-engage staff and identify gaps.

options.label: Tested over 3 years ago
options.feedback: Prioritise conducting a business continuity exercise to validate the plan remains fit for purpose. Start with a desktop exercise to identify critical gaps before progressing to more complex scenarios.

options.label: No
options.feedback: Establish a regular business continuity testing schedule, starting with a simple desktop exercise. Testing identifies gaps, builds staff familiarity, and provides confidence that the school can respond effectively to disruptions.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Confirm whether business continuity testing has occurred and review any documentation from previous exercises. If no testing has been conducted, schedule a desktop exercise to validate arrangements.

questions.text: Which communication channels does your school rely on during emergencies or critical incidents?
How confident are you in your school's ability to communicate within 30 minutes with families during an incident?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label:
1
Not confident at all
options.feedback: Review communication systems and processes to identify barriers to rapid family messaging. Ensure parent/guardian contact details are current, test the mass notification system regularly, and prepare pre-drafted message templates for common scenarios.

Review whether communication systems can reach all families quickly, confirm contact data is accurate and complete, and establish clear processes for who authorises and sends messages during incidents. Test arrangements regularly.

Identify specific barriers to faster family communication and address them — this may include system limitations, data quality, or unclear processes. Consider pre-drafted templates and regular testing to reduce response time.

Continue to maintain accurate contact data, test communication systems regularly, and refine messaging templates. Consider whether all scenarios are covered and whether backup communication methods exist if primary systems fail.

options.label:
5
Very confident
options.feedback: Maintain rapid family communication capability through regular testing, keeping contact data current, and reviewing message templates. Ensure backup communication methods are available and staff know how to activate them.

questions.text: Does your school have pre-prepared templates or protocols for communicating with families during incidents?
questions.scoringComment: Only add in one score item

options.label: Yes
options.feedback: Ensure communication templates cover a range of scenarios (emergency evacuation, lockdown, medical incident, operational disruptions, critical incidents) and are reviewed regularly for accuracy and tone. Confirm staff know where to access them and who has authority to approve and send communications. Establish, document, and test alternate communication channels to ensure messages can still be sent if primary systems are unavailable.

options.label: Partly
options.feedback: Expand the communication template library to cover additional scenarios. Include initial notification, update, and all-clear messages, holding statements, reception scripts, and website incident page scripts. Store templates in an accessible location and ensure multiple staff members can access them. Establish, document, and test alternate communication channels to ensure messages can still be sent if primary systems are unavailable.

options.label: No
options.feedback: Develop pre-prepared communication templates as a priority. Create templates for common scenarios including emergency evacuation, lockdown, medical incidents, and operational disruptions. Include placeholders for incident-specific details and ensure templates are easily accessible. Establish, document, and test alternate communication channels to ensure messages can still be sent if primary systems are unavailable.

options.label: Unsure
options.feedback: Confirm whether pre-prepared communication templates exist and where they are stored. If templates are available, ensure staff know how to access them. If not, develop templates for common incident scenarios. Establish, document, and test alternate communication channels to ensure messages can still be sent if primary systems are unavailable.
